text:
lina: Heads-up: I want to tighten decrypt perms for object-store snapshots. Proposal: new role `snapshot-decryptor`, KMS grants with 30m TTL, and EncryptionContext checks for `snapshot_id` + `project_id`. Putting this here for quick feedback.

omar: Sounds sensible. Any migration plan so running restores don't fail?

lina: Yes: run a CMK-tagging job, create grants proactively for queued restores, enable an enforcement canary for 24h, then switch enforcement. We'll not revoke existing broad grants until after 7 days of monitoring.

trent: How will we detect misuse? e.g., reuse of a grant across tenants?

lina: Audit events go to encops-audit; schema includes grant_id,key_id,requester,snapshot_id,project_id,action,result. Alerts: cross-project decrypts with same grant_id, or grant used outside its TTL.

omar: Also need access gating on the audit store. We can't leak tenant IDs to too many teams.

lina: Agreed. Audit raw events go to encrypted S3 restricted to sec-team SA. Metrics/alerts will be pushed to Datadog with PII redaction.

encops-bot: deploy-check: feature flag `snapshot_ttl_30m=true` added to staging. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/snapshot-decrypt-tightening

trent: add a smoke test that attempts decrypt with mismatched snapshot_id and expects deny. Also weekly scan for lingering broad grants.

lina: Will add tests + infra PR tomorrow. Thanks. :lock:
